title: Great Mosque of Djenne
blurb: The largest adobe building in the world: the 1907 Sudano-Sahelian mosque of Djenne with its three great minarets, ostrich-egg finials and palm-beam toron scaffolding, rebuilt every year by the whole town.

sourceUrls.label: Google Arts & Culture: The Great Mosque of Djenne

systems.name: Platform and stairs
systems.description: The 75 x 75 m platform raised 3 m against the Bani floods, with six pinnacled staircases.

systems.name: Qibla wall
systems.description: The east prayer wall with its segments, pilasters, merlons and doors.

systems.name: Minarets
systems.description: The three great box-like minarets of the qibla wall, the central about 16 m tall, each with a cone spire and an ostrich egg.

systems.name: Toron beams
systems.description: Bundles of rodier palm sticks protruding from the walls: decoration and permanent scaffolding for the annual replastering.

systems.name: Outer walls
systems.description: The north, south and west walls with their buttresses, merlons and doors.

systems.name: Prayer hall
systems.description: The prayer hall interior: nine walls of pillars, the roof with its vents, and the three mihrab niches.

systems.name: Courtyard
systems.description: The interior courtyard with galleries on three sides.
